title: Silver transport probe result v1
description:
Evidence that a transport actually responded, recorded by the agent that called it.

Silver never opens a socket, so for an MCP transport it can only ever establish `configured` — the host owns the connection. The agent can call the tool, and this is where it says what happened. Availability then reports `responding` only while a fresh, agreeing probe exists, which is the 0.7 rule applied to tools: a claimed pass with no evidence is not believed.

A probe is a measurement with a timestamp, not a permanent fact. It goes stale on purpose.

tool.description: The tool the agent actually called. Recorded so a probe against the wrong tool is visible rather than counted.

outcome.description: responded: the call returned something matching what the transport said to expect. failed: it was reached and did not work. refused: the call was declined — no permission, no authorization, or the tool is not in the agent's namespace at all.

detail.description: What came back, or what went wrong. This is what `--diagnose` shows a designer, so it should read like an answer rather than a stack trace.

recorded_by.description: Which agent made the call. A probe is somebody's observation, and an unattributed one cannot be weighed.
